title: Daily X narrative digest — 2026-10-27

hits.name: Anthony Pompliano 🌪
hits.text:
I have been thinking a lot about the rise of AI agents and how it will change the way we interact with internet products.

It feels like we have officially left the Internet 2.0 era and are now in the take-off phase of Internet 3.0.

The biggest change I see happening in our
hits.hook: I have been thinking a lot about the rise of AI agents and how it will change the way we interact with internet products.
hits.draft_en:
Everyone says AI agents will change the internet.
Ok. Will they change your $BTC process?
An agent can run a backtest in seconds. It can't tell you if the assumptions are garbage.
Tools scale. Bad logic scales too.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Fair take. But what's the evidence it's take-off and not another hype cycle?
Adoption numbers or vibes? Genuinely asking.
hits.video_tip: Talking head: 'AI can backtest. It can't think for you.' Show a quick backtest screen.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
BITCOIN MINER MARA SENDS 1,000 BTC TO BITGO, WORTH $80M.

Arkham claims it was a sale.

Business as usual, given they mine 800 BTC per month.

Nothing to worry about! https://t.co/GV21h7g6FH
hits.hook: BITCOIN MINER MARA SENDS 1,000 BTC TO BITGO, WORTH $80M.
hits.draft_en:
A miner sends 1,000 $BTC to a custodian and the feed calls it a sale.

Maybe it is. Miners sell to pay bills. That's normal.

But "Arkham claims" isn't confirmation. A transfer is a transfer until someone shows the trade.

Do you price this in, or wait for data?
hits.draft_quote_en:
"Arkham claims it was a sale." Has MARA confirmed it? Moving coins to a custodian and selling them aren't the same event.

And if it's ~1 month of output (their figure, verify), why is it headline news?
hits.video_tip: On-chain transfer graphic: wallet A to BitGo, with a big question mark on 'sold?'. 12s.

Vague hype gets engagement. It doesn't build a $BTC position.

hits.draft_en:
Google searches for Bitcoin at a 6-year low (their chart, verify).

"So it's time to accumulate."

Maybe. But low search interest also showed up before longer chops. Is this a timing signal or just a mood reading?

What's the forward $BTC return after past lows like this?
hits.draft_quote_en: Low retail interest has been a decent contrarian mood gauge. Has anyone measured the forward returns after it, with no look-ahead on when the low was 'the low'?
hits.video_tip: Google Trends line with past lows marked and what $BTC did in the next 90 days. 15s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:

Demand for bullish leverage stayed neutral.

Funding rate healthy between 6% and 11%. https://t.co/ZaJEiC63Vl
hits.hook: Retail traders far from desperate below $80K.
hits.draft_en:
Funding neutral. Leverage demand flat. Price under $80K.

Good. Less leverage means fewer forced sellers.

But calm funding isn't a buy signal by itself. It just tells you who isn't panicking yet.

Spot only. No leverage. No shorts. $BTC
hits.draft_quote_en: Healthy funding is a good sign for spot holders. Does it actually lead price, or just describe it? Would like to see the lag.
hits.video_tip: Funding rate chart with the 6-11% band shaded, $BTC price on top. 15s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
Coinbase CEO: You can invent more gold and diamonds.

You can’t invent more Bitcoin. Only 21 million will ever exist. https://t.co/ZXQ3Ga7YfT
hits.hook: Coinbase CEO: You can invent more gold and diamonds.
hits.draft_en:
"You can't invent more Bitcoin."

True for supply. Not true for exposure.

Paper claims, ETFs and IOUs can multiply. Only coins you hold with your own keys are part of the 21M you actually own.

Which $BTC do you have?
hits.draft_quote_en: Fixed supply is the easy part. The question is how much of the claims on $BTC are backed 1:1 and withdrawable.
hits.video_tip: Text animation: 21,000,000 then 'your keys?' 10s.

hits.name: glassnode
hits.text:
Our backtesting engine found this bitcoin:native rule.

It buys when the 30-day RSI of entities in profit crosses above its threshold.

Since July 2023, its worst drawdown was 20%, against 53% for holding.

Discover your own strategy 👇
https://t.co/UnQWDO1QGx https://t.co/rQeS0pLFUF
hits.hook: Our backtesting engine found this bitcoin:native rule.
hits.draft_en:
"Worst drawdown 20% vs 53% for holding."

Since July 2023. One rule, one window, found by an engine that searched for it.

How many rules did it test before this one? What happens before 2023? Costs included?

A rule found by search needs out-of-sample data before I trust it with $BTC.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Interesting rule. How many candidates did the engine try before surfacing this one, and how does it do on data before July 2023?

Without that, a 20% vs 53% drawdown could be fit, not edge.
hits.video_tip: Screen-record: equity curve from 2023, then extend it back to 2018 and see if the edge holds. Say 'verify' if you can't. 20s.

hits.name: Pledditor
hits.text:
3 big sins:
1. For years, their marketing falsely claimed that all PII was being deleted when it actually wasn't
2. Starting May this year, they silently changed the ToS and began to knowingly store PII, but didn't announce these changes to the customer
3. And it all got hacked https://t.co/nNWixt6sqi
hits.hook: 3 big sins:
hits.draft_en:
A wallet company can protect your keys and still leak your name and address.

Different risks. Most people only think about the first one.

What's your plan if your vendor's customer list ends up public?
hits.draft_quote_en: Which company is this, for people reading along? And is there a confirmed scope of the leak yet, or only reports?
hits.video_tip: Short checklist on screen: PO box, separate email, pay privately, verify firmware. 15s.

hits.name: Pledditor
hits.text: Hardware wallets are super low-tech devices running extremely simple firmware. The only ongoing demand users have of the manufacturer is not to leak their data to bad actors. That the bitcoin space has fumbled something so basic is deeply embarrassing. You are not serious people.
hits.hook: Hardware wallets are super low-tech devices running extremely simple firmware. The only ongoing demand users have of the manufacturer is not to leak their data to bad actors. That the bitcoin space has fumbled something so basic is deeply embarrassing. You are not serious people.
hits.draft_en:
Your hardware wallet doesn't need to know who you are.

The device signs. Your shipping address, email and order history are the weak spot.

Buy with privacy in mind. Air-gapped signing helps the keys. It doesn't fix the customer database.

What data did you hand over to buy yours?
hits.draft_quote_en:
Agree. The keys can be fine and the customer list can still be the leak.

Which is why I'd rather minimize what the vendor knows about me in the first place.
hits.video_tip: Two boxes on screen: 'keys (offline)' vs 'customer data (vendor)'. Cross the second. 12s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
Bitcoin expected to hit $537K by 2030 and $1.48M by 2034 according to Monte Carlo simulation.

🟠🚀  🟠🚀

95% probability of $200K+ by 2030. 150% upside.

🫡 @sminston_with https://t.co/GfveLlSNyW
hits.hook: Bitcoin expected to hit $537K by 2030 and $1.48M by 2034 according to Monte Carlo simulation.
hits.draft_en:
"$537K by 2030. 95% probability of $200K+."

A Monte Carlo is only as good as the assumptions you feed it.

Change the volatility or the drift a little and the 'probability' moves a lot.

What inputs did they use? Has anyone checked?
hits.draft_quote_en:
What drift and volatility went into this? Monte Carlo doesn't predict $BTC, it just restates your inputs with nicer charts.

Would love to see the sensitivity table.
hits.video_tip: Run a quick Monte Carlo twice on screen with slightly different vol; show how the 'target' jumps. 20s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Magazine

JUST IN: Casa's Chief Security Officer Jameson Lopp says Bitcoin faces no immediate threat from quantum computing. 👀

"We are orders of magnitudes away from a real usable quantum computer that can crack the algorithm that is used to secure your Bitcoin." 👏 https://t.co/dr2A9o6qL4

hits.draft_en:
"Orders of magnitude away" from a quantum computer that can break $BTC.

Probably true. Still worth asking: what's the upgrade plan, and who moves first?

No panic. No denial. Just a timeline and a plan.
hits.draft_quote_en: Agree on the timeline. But "no immediate threat" isn't "no threat." What happens to old coins with exposed public keys when it does get close?
hits.video_tip: Whiteboard 20s: 'how far are we?' with qubits needed vs qubits today (cite the source, verify).

hits.name: Bitcoin Magazine
hits.text:
JUST IN: Bitcoin has entered an accumulation phase, according to Galaxy Research. 👀

"We think the bear market ended in June and that bitcoin is in the accumulation phase that has preceded every prior advance." 🚀 https://t.co/X3OwAZ8rpX
hits.hook: JUST IN: Bitcoin has entered an accumulation phase, according to Galaxy Research. 👀
hits.story: Galaxy: accumulation phase / bottom is in
hits.draft_en:
"The bear market ended in June."

Maybe. But "accumulation phase" is a label you can only confirm after the advance shows up.

What's the rule that called it in June, in real time? And how often did the same rule fire too early?

$BTC doesn't care about the label.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Accumulation according to which metric, and with what false-positive rate?

If "every prior advance" was preceded by this phase, how many times did the phase show up and no advance followed?
hits.video_tip: Put the Galaxy quote on screen, then a $BTC chart with past 'accumulation' calls, misses included. 20s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Magazine
hits.text:
JUST IN: Coinbase Institutional Co-CEO says they enable JPMorgan, Citi, and PNC to let clients buy BTC directly in banking apps.

“If I can do that with hundreds...thousands of clients, then we've activated the whole US in order to facilitate everyone's ability to buy Bitcoin" 🚀 https://t.co/kWTK3WpLr6
hits.hook: JUST IN: Coinbase Institutional Co-CEO says they enable JPMorgan, Citi, and PNC to let clients buy BTC directly in banking apps.

hits.draft_en:

Can you withdraw to your own wallet? Who holds the keys? What does the spread cost you?

Easy access isn't the same as ownership.
hits.draft_quote_en: Big distribution win. One question: can those bank clients withdraw to self-custody, or is it an IOU with a $BTC ticker on it?
hits.video_tip: Split screen: bank app 'buy' button vs a hardware wallet receive address. 15s, one question on screen.
